catalog_quote: [Renck 1975 sec. 1.1.3] Three tones may be observed in Yagaria, low, mid, and high. But only two minimal word pairs have been discovered which contrast by mid and low tones, so that the existence of two tonemes may be stated: /'ve/ 'man', /'ve/ 'spirit', /ha'li/ 'fire', /ha'li/ 'arrow'. But this basis obviously is too narrow to establish Yagaria as a tone language. In all other cases where the occurrence of minimal pairs depends on suprasegments, stress is the decisive factor, and the occurring tone is closely linked with stress: /'havu/ 'root', /ha'vu/ 'bow', /'gaena/ 'line', /ga'ena/ 'penis'. There are three emic degrees of stress: Stress, non-stress, and reduction. The last degree results in the occurrence of "reduced" syllables in which quite often the vowel is hardly audible. ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: the deciding passages are in the held Renck 1975 (PL B-40 sec. 1.1.3 p.12, sec. 1.4 p.15) and Renck 1967 (PL A-12 pp.40-42, 46-47) text layers at the stated locators, verbatim modulo de-spacing of the letter-spaced scanned layer. The deciding source is a genuine reference grammar (1975) plus the author's phoneme paper (1967), and the author's 1977 dictionary (downloaded now, PL C-37 p.xii) repeats the analysis, so within Renck's work the record is solid. But it is not the whole literature: (a) Glottolog's top grammar, Haiman 1980 Hua (550 pp), is unheld and paywalled; (b) Ford 1993 (open, downloaded and scanned now), based on new fieldwork on Move, Huva, Yate, Kami and Kafe with tones verified by whistling, analyses Kamano-Yagaria as 'a lexical tone language' with H/L (and Extra-high) tones, HL vs LH word patterns in Move, stable/unstable final tones and tone sandhi, and never me

sources.quote: 'Stress in emic in Yagaria. There are minimal pairs contrasting in stress only, e.g., /'havu/ root, /ha'vu/ bow, /'fayana/ fish, /fa'yana/ design. ... in the main Yagaria entries, all polysyllabic words except affixes carry one main word stress indicated by the accent'; 'Tone, which is actually not emic, and has been observed as a contrastive feature with two word pairs only, is not indicated'; p.xiv 'every word contains one, and only one, main stress'. (Accent marks do not survive in the text layer, so no positional count was attempted.)
